label: accepted

evidence.V1: Doorway reads from front, three-quarter and silhouette (through-opening visible); centred in the panel.
evidence.V2: Clear: wall slab, medium door frame/lintel/cap/plinth, small gold keystone and chamfers.
evidence.V3: Squared stones and a plain rectangular opening with a raised threshold; functional but stiff.
evidence.V4: Uniform chamfers on stones, frame, lintel and keystone catch the light in lintel and doorway close-ups.
evidence.V5: Doorway, lintel and end-section close-ups clean; no pinches or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone greys in 3 values, light frame, single gold keystone accent - disciplined.
evidence.V7: 540 tris vs module target 800 - under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material, stone hue, gold keystone, consistent chamfers - matches modular kit.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Default collision so the doorway stays walkable, CanTouch off, Color white, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes.

evidence.V1: Doorway hole reads in the silhouette and front; the 3/4 reads as a walk-through door wall from every angle.
evidence.V2: Big wall slab, medium jamb stones / lintel course / door frame, small gold keystone - clear three tiers.
evidence.V3: Wall and jambs are good chunky stylised stone, but the doorway is a tall plain rectangle with a very thin uniform trim frame; reads somewhat stiff/primitive.
evidence.V4: Stones and cap have consistent chamfers that catch light, but the gold keystone is an unbevelled razor-edged trapezoid (lintel_studio/flat) and the frame bevel is very small, so treatment is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Doorway, lintel and end-section close-ups are clean; no pinches, seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone in three values plus a gold keystone accent; brick/slate colourways keep the structure.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, stone hue with gold keystone as specified for the modular kit, chamfered blocks.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default (keeps doorway walkable), CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling pass (iou 0.99).

evidence.V1: Doorway reads from front, three-quarter and silhouette (opening punched through, centred); top view is a clean bar as expected for a wall module.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: slab, cap ledge and plinth (big), block piers, lintel and door frame (medium), gold keystone (small).
evidence.V3: Sound proportions and a centred opening, but blocks are uniform rectangles and the frame is a thin flat band; partly stylised rather than confident.
evidence.V4: Consistent small chamfers on blocks, frame, threshold and cap ledge that catch light in the doorway, lintel and end close-ups.
evidence.V5: Doorway, lintel and end-section close-ups (studio and flat) show clean flat shading; no pinches, seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Stone grey in about 3 values plus a single gold keystone accent; brick and basalt colourways keep the value structure.
evidence.V7: 540 tris vs module target 800, under target.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material, stone hue values, gold keystone accent and kit-scale chamfers; matches the modular kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct (anchored, Default collision keeps the doorway walkable, CanTouch off, white colour, grid-corner pivot); T1 tiling pass with iou 0.989.

artifacts: Keystone has no chamfer, reads razor-sharp against the bevelled stones
keystone slightly overhangs the lintel's lower edge into the opening (lintel close-up); reads as intended but borderline
top_fixes: Lower or flush the threshold so the walkway is floor-level
Add a stronger lintel or voussoir stones above the frame for hierarchy
Vary stone sizes in the jambs
Chamfer the keystone and enlarge it slightly (or make it a real voussoir in the lintel course) so it reads at 64 px
Give the door frame more depth/width or replace it with stone jamb blocks + a proper lintel so the opening is less of a plain rectangle
Consider a slightly arched or stepped head to add stylised character
Give the door surround more stylised weight: thicker projecting jambs/lintel or an arched head, with block-cut voussoirs
Vary pier block sizes and add a small tier (chipped corner, iron hinge pins in ink) for richer detail
Dress the exposed end section with block returns for wall-run terminations
